title: Continuity of the open-proper-closed composite on the ambient localizing hull
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside it, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$, or $\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with exactly the discrete or induced $\ell$-adic topological condensed-ring convention of [sk-def-localizing-closure]. For every scheme $T$ put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ and $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T})$, the ordinary unbounded module-object derived category [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], with smallness fixed by [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme, let $q:Y\to S$ and $f:X\to Y$ be proper morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], let $e:V\hookrightarrow X$ be a quasi-compact open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $c:C\hookrightarrow Y$ be a closed immersion with quasi-compact open complement [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For any scheme $T$ write $\mathcal L_T=\operatorname{Loc}(\mathrm D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(T,\Lambda))$, with finite constant scalar-model constructibility and Tor amplitude as in [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and with the replete triangulated closure and small coproducts taken in the ambient $D_T$ [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Put $J=D(e_!)$ [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek]. The actual module-object inverse images $e^*$ and $c^*$ have underlying functors the ordinary exact inverse images of abelian sheaves, and are exact. The derived functors $J$ and $D(c^*)$ are triangulated and preserve all small ambient coproducts. Moreover, $J(\mathcal L_V)\subseteq\mathcal L_X$, and the functor
$$F=D(c^*)\circ Rf_*\circ J:\mathcal L_V\longrightarrow D_C$$
is triangulated and preserves all small ambient coproducts. Explicitly, for every small family $(K_t)_{t\in I}$ of objects of $\mathcal L_V$, the canonical map
$$\bigoplus_{t\in I}F(K_t)\longrightarrow F\!\left(\bigoplus_{t\in I}K_t\right)$$
is an isomorphism, including $I=\varnothing$, without common cohomological bounds or a derived-completeness condition. No relation between the images of $e$ and $c$ is required, and no vanishing assertion is made. There is no field, characteristic, Noetherian or finite-dimensional-base hypothesis.

proof.text: For $T=V,X,Y,C$, abelian pro-etale sheaves form a closed symmetric monoidal Grothendieck category by [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed]. Applying [lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck] to the commutative ring object $\Lambda_T$ makes $\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T}$ Grothendieck. Hence it has small coproducts and K-injective resolutions, as supplied by [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. These are the ambient categories used throughout.

proof.text: Apply the untwisted assertion of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] to $e$ and $c$: their actual scalar-extension module inverse images are canonically the lifts of ordinary abelian inverse image and are exact. By [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek], $e_!$ is exact and left adjoint to $e^*$. The exact-functor theorem [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] therefore makes $J=D(e_!)$ and $D(c^*)$ triangulated termwise functors.

proof.text: The adjunctions $e_!\dashv e^*$ and $c^*\dashv c_*$ are given by [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] and [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] applied to a small discrete index category says both underived left adjoints preserve every small coproduct. Apply [lem-pur-exact-derived-coproducts] to these exact functors between the Grothendieck categories of step 1. It follows that $J$ and $D(c^*)$ preserve the ambient unbounded derived coproducts, including the empty one; no restriction on degrees is involved.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-qc-open-extension-ctf] to send the finite constant-model constructible finite-Tor generators under J into the target generators. For any replete localizing target property P containing those generators, its inverse image along J is triangulated and replete by Mathlib ObjectProperty.inverseImage. It is closed under the specified small coproducts: J preserves the diagram colimit by step 3, and the inverse of preservesColimitIso transports the target closure assertion back to J of that colimit. The defining intersection localizingClosureOfSize then sends every source hull object into P, hence into the target hull. The source hull is triangulated directly: zero and shifts belong to every defining property, and for a distinguished triangle whose first and third objects lie in the intersection, each defining replete triangulated property contains the middle object. Its inclusion is therefore triangulated by Mathlib.

proof.text:
For the given $S,q,f$, [lem-sfb-qcqs-proper-localizing-coproducts] applies without further hypotheses to every small family $(JK_t)$ in $\mathcal L_X$ supplied by step 4. Its canonical proper coproduct comparison is invertible. The K-injective right derived functor $Rf_*$ is triangulated by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. Thus the composite $F$ on $\mathcal L_V$ is triangulated. For sums its comparison factors as the following three canonical isomorphisms:
$$\bigoplus_tD(c^*)Rf_*JK_t\ \cong\ D(c^*)\bigl(\bigoplus_tRf_*JK_t\bigr)\ \cong\ D(c^*)Rf_*\bigl(\bigoplus_tJK_t\bigr)\ \cong\ D(c^*)Rf_*J\bigl(\bigoplus_tK_t\bigr).$$
Each composite with the $t$-th coprojection is $F$ of that coprojection, so this is exactly the comparison asked for. The same factorization holds for the empty index set. The proper theorem has neither a common bound nor a completeness assumption, and the other two functors act on the full ambient categories. Consequently no relation between the images of $e,c$ or additional geometric hypothesis is used.

The statement and stmt_deps are unchanged from the Q139 unsplit node. Each step uses only what its cited statements say. Step 1: lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed plus lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck make Mod_{Λ_T} Grothendieck, and sk-def-sfb-derived-categories gives K-injective resolutions. Step 2: the untwisted clause of sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients makes the module inverse images exact, sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek gives e_! exact with e_! ⊣ e^*, and lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated makes the derived functors triangulated. Step 3: c^* ⊣ c_* from the module pushforward-pullback node, lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits on a discrete index category, and lem-pur-exact-derived-coproducts (its hypotheses checked) give ambient sum preservation. Step 4: lem-sfb-qc-open-extension-ctf (same unit, exact coefficient and constructibility conventions, quasi-compact open hypothesis) plus det-proper-image-localizing-principle give J(L_V) ⊆ L_X. Step 5: lem-sfb-qcqs-proper-localizing-coproducts has exactly the item's scope (S qcqs, q and f proper, I=∅ included, no bounds). With it, the 3-isomorphism factorization and the coprojection check correctly give the canonical comparison. Sources checked: blueprint main-20261015 det-sf-comp-coherence-refinement proof (2), first paragraph; Stacks 07D9, 015F, 0038 at the right labels; no SGA. Edge cases checked: I=∅, V=∅, e=id, C=∅, overlapping images of e and c, residue characteristic ℓ; c's quasi-compact-complement hypothesis is unused but harmless. Not duplicates: det-sf-comp-coherence-single and det-proper-image-localizing-open are restricted to finite-type schemes over a field. No cycle. The off-unit generic tools declared in split_report.tool_uses are accepted. Batch-5: lem-sfb-qcqs-proper-localizing-coproducts reaches lem-pod-lisse-module-sheaves-as-module-objects only through proper base change. That node is the foundational fact that lisse sheaves are module objects in finite locally constant étale sheaves; it is not the content or a step of Poincaré duality or the trace formula, and neither assumption leaf gives it. The cited proper-coproduct property is also outside both assumptions, so there is no RETURN.
